Private credential ownership: Personal credentials are identity-scoped secret-store records; selection checks canonical ownership, and credential plus default-link writes occur together after the live assertion inside the synchronous transaction.

Addressed all actionable findings in 68cda1fb660 (head of this PR):

- **[P1] Manual links restricted** — `users.linkAuthProfile` is now `operator.admin` only, with the guidance error pointing non-admins at the self-service connect flows (which prove account control). The profile page hides the manual row for non-admin writers. Cross-credential denial is covered by a unit test and by a live-gateway probe (redacted trace in the PR body): a write-scoped user linking `openai:scott` gets `FORBIDDEN`, the same identity with `operator.admin` succeeds.
- **Reconnect overwrite amplification closed** — a reconnect reuses the linked auth profile id only when the stored credential carries the same provider `accountId`; anything else (including setup-token credentials, which carry no comparable identity) mints a fresh id, so a link aimed at a shared or foreign credential can never be clobbered. Regression: "mints a fresh id when the linked profile stores a different provider account".
- **[P2] Lazy storage honored on reads** — `users.listAuthLinks` and unlink now read through the existing read-only helper and return empty when the table is absent; only the first real link creates it. Regression proves list+unlink on a fresh database leave the table uncreated.
- **Post-exchange revalidation** — authority is re-checked after the awaited OAuth exchange and before any persistence: the RPC path re-runs the caller's live access predicate, and both paths fail closed when the person's profile no longer resolves. Regressions: "rejects completion when authority is revoked during the token exchange" (revocation happens inside the awaited exchange; no credential write, no link write) and "fails closed when the person's profile disappears before persistence".
- **SQLite table** — the additive `user_profile_auth_links` table was explicitly approved in the operator's chat before implementation (new STRICT table, no schema-version bump, downgraded readers unaffected); the read paths above now also guarantee it never appears on gateways that never link.

PR body's Evidence section is updated with the redacted live authority-chain traces and the new regression coverage.

**Rewrite update — `406558d37965a44ee160963f865db4aeee79052e` (not merged).** Thanks @scoootscooob for the original feature and tests. The rewrite addresses the six original-head findings below: private identity-owned credentials replace shared-pool writes; ChatGPT replacement checks user plus workspace; Gateway-owned sign-in revalidates live authority, contains callback failures, and supports acknowledged cancellation; Profile refresh no longer owns account-operation cleanup.

**Best-fix verdict:** the rewrite puts credential ownership and sign-in lifetime at their authoritative boundaries. Keeping private credentials in the shared store with downstream filters leaves ownership ambiguous; adding another table would duplicate the existing secret-store capability. Reviewed paths include the [identity-owned account store](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/406558d37965a44ee160963f865db4aeee79052e/src/state/user-model-accounts.ts), [Gateway operation owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/406558d37965a44ee160963f865db4aeee79052e/src/gateway/model-account-connect.ts), [session selection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/406558d37965a44ee160963f865db4aeee79052e/src/agents/auth-profiles/session-override.ts), and [Profile account state](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/406558d37965a44ee160963f865db4aeee79052e/ui/src/pages/profile/model-accounts.ts), alongside callers, siblings, tests, and the Codex contracts cited below.

Production scope against captured main: **+3,073/-456 (net +2,617)**; tests **+2,698/-192**. Growth implements the private-account feature and its owner/lifecycle boundaries; test support, generated clients, and docs are counted separately in the PR body.

The final frozen candidate passed **1,144 tests across 49 files**, plus **9 Chromium E2E cases** with a fresh UI build and mock Gateway. The final scoped independent review returned zero actionable P0–P2 findings across both review chunks. Review-driven regressions also cover session-pin precedence and preserving newer links when replaying an OAuth result. The `ciArtifacts` runtime/SDK/UI build, export checks, and bundle budgets passed. All selected checks passed across the original run and its recorded continuation. One unchanged `test/scripts/mac-elevation-artifact.test.ts` case hit its 20-second limit initially; the same group passed all 530 tests on rerun without code, concurrency, or timeout changes. The isolated normal-Gateway/browser run passed four checks covering ChatGPT start/cancel, synthetic Claude credential linking, persistence after page reload, and unlink. Two metadata-change events; zero browser errors.

Remaining validation includes real-provider sign-in/inference and exact-pushed-head CI. The updated PR body separates synthetic proof from the author's original-head live-provider reports and records the storage/ownership changes, media, and remaining limits. Shared failover and sticky collaborator/fork selection remain intentional; this is not a per-turn billing guarantee or tenant-isolation feature. No merge approval or exact-pushed-head CI result is implied.

The original review below is preserved as the record of findings against `f6e71a27e2dd11c9406bba1e5747ab0ca21ffb6d`, not an assessment of the rewritten head.

---

<details>
<summary>Original-head review — findings addressed by the rewrite</summary>

Source review of head `f6e71a27e2dd11c9406bba1e5747ab0ca21ffb6d`: the per-person account feature makes sense, but the current implementation has these actionable ownership/lifecycle issues. A maintainer rewrite is in progress; this is not a merge approval.

1. **P1 — Personal credentials enter the gateway's automatic account pool.** Both connect paths write ordinary shared-store profiles. With no explicit auth order or configured profile list, the existing selector considers every stored provider credential and favors fresh OAuth credentials. An unrelated, unlinked session can therefore select the new personal account without any failover. Unlink removes only the association, so the credential remains eligible. The owner needs a distinction between personal credentials and shared automatic/failover candidates, retained after unlink. [Connect write](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f6e71a27e2dd11c9406bba1e5747ab0ca21ffb6d/src/gateway/server-methods/users-auth-connect.ts#L219), [default selection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f6e71a27e2dd11c9406bba1e5747ab0ca21ffb6d/src/agents/auth-profiles/order.ts#L290).

2. **P1 — Same ChatGPT workspace does not prove the same OAuth user.** Reconnect replaces a linked credential when its `accountId` matches. Upstream Codex distinguishes `chatgpt_account_id` (organization/workspace) from `chatgpt_user_id`. Two members of one workspace can pass that comparison, allowing a reconnect to overwrite a shared/foreign linked profile and change the credential used by other pinned sessions. Compare the provider subject and workspace, or enforce separately recorded credential ownership; permission to use a linked credential is not permission to replace it. [Replacement check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f6e71a27e2dd11c9406bba1e5747ab0ca21ffb6d/src/gateway/server-methods/users-auth-connect.ts#L150), [directly inspected Codex contract](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/bc39b0ed59a85c47b2e9c267cdd57bb1018bc5f2/codex-rs/login/src/token_data.rs#L35).

3. **P1 — Post-exchange revalidation misses actual revocation.** `canMutateProfile` trusts retained scopes/profile identity and ignores connection invalidation. A role change invalidates the connection without replacing those retained fields, and an ordinary in-flight RPC can finish after its socket closes. The automatic callback retains no initiating authority check at all. The new revocation test changes a mocked identity resolver instead of exercising the real invalidation mechanism. Both completion transports need the same live flow-authority check before persistence. [Completion check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f6e71a27e2dd11c9406bba1e5747ab0ca21ffb6d/src/gateway/server-methods/users-auth-connect.ts#L420).

4. **P1 — Callback persistence failures can terminate the gateway.** The HTTP listener launches the callback promise without a rejection handler. A credential-store lock failure is wrapped in a generic error and can escape to the fatal unhandled-rejection handler. The paste-RPC sibling catches failures, while the HTTP sibling does not. Every HTTP failure needs a redacted terminal response and guaranteed cleanup. [Callback listener](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f6e71a27e2dd11c9406bba1e5747ab0ca21ffb6d/src/gateway/server-methods/users-auth-connect.ts#L287).

5. **P2 — Cancel only clears the browser state.** Start ChatGPT sign-in, open its tab, return to Profile and cancel, then finish the already-open sign-in: the still-pending server flow stores and links the account. Polling has stopped, so the page can keep displaying no linked account. Cancellation must retire the exact server operation, including completion already awaiting an exchange. [Cancel handler](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f6e71a27e2dd11c9406bba1e5747ab0ca21ffb6d/ui/src/pages/profile/profile-page.ts#L655).

6. **P2 — Profile Refresh can leave Model accounts permanently busy.** While an account RPC is outstanding, Refresh remains enabled and increments `identityRequestId`. The account operation then skips its busy-state cleanup, leaving all account controls disabled until the component reconnects/reloads. Account operations need lifecycle ownership independent of profile identity refresh. [Cleanup](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f6e71a27e2dd11c9406bba1e5747ab0ca21ffb6d/ui/src/pages/profile/profile-page.ts#L531).

The coherent repair is to retain the useful person-to-account link and session pinning, while making credential ownership and pending authorization lifecycle explicit. Current main's personal GitHub connection flow (#133799) provides an adjacent pattern for live authority, exact operation identity, cancellation, and terminal status. Provider-specific identity comparison belongs to the provider owner.

Billing policy also needs precise wording: ordered same-provider failover can charge another account, and forks inherit their parent's pin. These are product choices, not an unconditional session-owner-pays guarantee.

Evidence: source/test review across connect handlers, shared-store upserts, auth ordering, session selection, profile UI, current-main siblings, and upstream Codex token/callback contracts. No independent runtime or live-billing rerun was performed for this review. Exact-head CI passed at the reviewed head. Production delta: +1,831/-167 (net +1,664); tests +1,214/-8, with test support, docs, generated files, and tooling counted separately.

</details>

Upstream Codex distinguishes `chatgpt_account_id` (organization/workspace) from `chatgpt_user_id`. Two members of one workspace can pass that comparison, allowing a reconnect to overwrite a shared/foreign linked profile and change the credential used by other pinned sessions. Compare the provider subject and workspace, or enforce separately recorded credential ownership; permission to use a linked credential is not permission to replace it. A role change invalidates the connection without replacing those retained fields, and an ordinary in-flight RPC can finish after its socket closes. The automatic callback retains no initiating authority check at all. The new revocation test changes a mocked identity resolver instead of exercising the real invalidation mechanism. A credential-store lock failure is wrapped in a generic error and can escape to the fatal unhandled-rejection handler. The paste-RPC sibling catches failures, while the HTTP sibling does not. Every HTTP failure needs a redacted terminal response and guaranteed cleanup. [Callback listener](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f6e71a27e2dd11c9406bba1e5747ab0ca21ffb6d/src/gateway/server-methods/users-auth-connect.ts#L287).

5. **P2 — Cancel only clears the browser state.** Start ChatGPT sign-in, open its tab, return to Profile and cancel, then finish the already-open sign-in: the still-pending server flow stores and links the account. Polling has stopped, so the page can keep displaying no linked account. Cancellation must retire the exact server operation, including completion already awaiting an exchange. [Cancel handler](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f6e71a27e2dd11c9406bba1e5747ab0ca21ffb6d/ui/src/pages/profile/profile-page.ts#L655).

6. **P2 — Profile Refresh can leave Model accounts permanently busy.** While an account RPC is outstanding, Refresh remains enabled and increments `identityRequestId`. The account operation then skips its busy-state cleanup, leaving all account controls disabled until the component reconnects/reloads. Account operations need lifecycle ownership independent of profile identity refresh. Current main's personal GitHub connection flow (#133799) provides an adjacent pattern for live authority, exact operation identity, cancellation, and terminal status. Provider-specific identity comparison belongs to the provider owner.

Evidence: source/test review across connect handlers, shared-store upserts, auth ordering, session selection, profile UI, current-main siblings, and upstream Codex token/callback contracts. No independent runtime or live-billing rerun was performed for this review. Exact-head CI passed at the reviewed head. Production delta: +1,831/-167 (net +1,664); tests +1,214/-8, with test support, docs, generated files, and tooling counted separately.

</details>

Pushed the follow-up rewrite in 912f738198223be74286181528ac5902e068e460 and updated the PR description, docs, and before/after evidence. The PR remains open; this is not a merge approval.

The central design is now explicit: **saved account, new-chat default, chat selection, and temporary sign-in attempt are different things**. Profile, the personal-account CLI, and the chat picker share the Gateway-owned operations. Clearing a default does not delete the credential or rewrite existing chats. Custodian hands the person to protected controls where administrator access and working configured inference are available; it does not request credentials in conversation or grant an agent the person's sign-in authority.

Both concrete P1s from the [latest ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/134970#issuecomment-5490629462) are addressed. Ordinary replies now resolve the session's personal-account pin through its owning store instead of treating it as missing. Fresh selections require the authenticated human on the exact live connection, before credential/provider I/O and again at the canonical session write after awaited work. Inherited shared-session/fork pins remain valid; they are not fresh authority. This keeps the repair at selection and persistence boundaries rather than adding downstream retries or clearing pins to hide the mismatch.

Live verification also caught a profile-notification loop: avatar authentication performed an unchanged profile lookup, which published a profile change, which refreshed sessions and loaded the avatar again. Publication now follows actual writes inside the existing transaction owner. The unconditional wrapper is removed, the repair is net −4 production lines, and no UI throttle, cache, SQL/schema change, or retention/configuration option was added. The final built-Gateway browser run showed one real profile edit, one observer profile event and refresh, persistence after reload, and quiet 2.5-second windows before and after.

Verification includes 1,388 selected tests, 73 CLI startup sibling tests, 59 final profile/alias tests, 16 built-UI Playwright cases, Android/Swift lint, 1,038 macOS tooling tests, the selected type/boundary/schema guards, and a complete `ciArtifacts` build. The latest independent Codex review was scoped-clean within its **P0-only** remit. A source-blind normal-built-Gateway run additionally proved two-person ownership, CLI/UI default parity, sticky chat pins, foreign-account denial, and 53-account pagination (50 + 3). Fixture/setup failures and reruns are recorded in the updated body rather than described as an all-first-attempt pass.

The remaining Rank-up work is **not waived**: actual provider OAuth exchange, valid late-completion/revocation proof with working credentials, billed inference, applicable security-owner acceptance of the trust/billing model, and required exact-head CI/reviews remain prerequisites to a later merge. The source-blind Custodian conversation was blocked by its inference/owner prerequisites, so a genuine conversational handoff is not claimed verified. The account label is a selection, not a billing receipt; same-provider shared failover remains. Broader personal-inference startup, the separate main-reset model-forwarding trace, and the source-bootstrap catalog stall are named follow-ups in the PR body, not claimed fixed here.

Thanks to @scoootscooob for the original implementation and tests; contributor credit is preserved. @clawsweeper re-review

Live follow-up on 912f738198223be74286181528ac5902e068e460: **the configured-inference Custodian conversation and ordinary chat now have real-provider proof**, using actual Chrome and an isolated normal built Gateway.

A natural-language account-management request produced two real OpenAI Responses calls with `gpt-5.6-luna`, both HTTP 200 with terminal SSE completion. After 2,689 ms the Gateway returned `action: "none"` plus `handoff.kind: "model-accounts"`, and Chrome automatically opened Profile. No account-mutation or config-write RPCs occurred in that observed window.

Ordinary chat separately returned `LIVE_OK` in 3 seconds (20 output tokens). Its owner receipt recorded one normal attempt, zero retries/account rotations, and no failure, timeout, or abort. HTTP/SSE details were retained for the Custodian calls, not this ordinary-chat turn. The known provider key was absent from the captured logs, config, and RPC observation files.

**Still unverified:** personal ChatGPT OAuth exchange, Claude subscription-token inference, valid late OAuth completion, and account-specific billing. The real OpenAI login page requires human sign-in; an API key is not a substitute for those personal-account flows. The PR remains open and unmerged, with security-owner acceptance and required CI/reviews still needed before merge. The body now distinguishes the new live proof from the earlier source-blind fixture limits.

![Real-provider chat and Custodian handoff; synthetic identities and messages only](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/49d8dc2d-d68c-43cc-b321-936e0c8198fc)

Additional live proof on `912f738198223be74286181528ac5902e068e460`; no source changes during this run. The PR remains open—this is a verification update, not merge approval.

**Personal OpenAI OAuth + MFA now passed**, followed by three real interactive `gpt-5.6-luna` replies through Chrome and a normal built Gateway with no shared provider credentials. The seven-operation CLI roundtrip passed. Clearing the default kept the existing chat working; a fresh unselected chat returned 401 without advancing the personal account's success timestamp. Explicitly selecting the retained account restored eligible models and a successful reply while the new-chat default stayed cleared. Owner success bookkeeping corroborated each successful personal turn; it is not billing proof.

A second synthetic Gateway identity could neither see nor select that account; both inventories/defaults stayed unchanged after rejection. The original default was restored. The temporary Gateway, credential store, and task-owned runtime processes were cleaned up afterward.

![Live personal chat and sticky selection after clearing the default](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f50126e9-da46-498d-953a-cff5955de018)

**Still unverified:** Claude subscription-token inference, invoice/account-specific billing, and live same-provider shared failover. The additional late-callback probe got a cancel acknowledgement, but the second MFA UI flow did not complete and no callback arrived: **not a passed test of rejecting a valid late callback**. In-flight exchange cancellation and original-socket disconnect were not forced live.

Named UX follow-up: replace the fresh Automatic chat's raw 401 with actionable recovery guidance to **Account for this chat** or **Settings → Profile → Model accounts**, preserving the deliberate cleared default. Applicable security-owner acceptance, resolution of the current merge conflicts, and required exact-head CI/reviews remain before any later merge. Thanks again to @scoootscooob for the original contribution.

## New session account picker added and live-tested

Pushed **`a71936cce2ce94023114437eb321ecdbf0b44335`** to this PR. The previously recorded fresh-draft gap is closed: **Account for this chat** now sits inside New session's model picker. Choosing a saved account affects only the new chat, not the person's new-chat default.

The repair keeps the existing owners: draft selection is ephemeral UI state, model preview is an owner-authorized read, and creation uses the existing `model@account` contract. It reuses the chat control and catalog owner. It does not make all retained credentials automatically available, bypass readiness, persist private account IDs in preferences, or temporarily switch the default to make creation succeed.

**Real Claude proof on this exact head:** with the default cleared, native Claude logged out, and no shared credential, selecting the saved account exposed Haiku and enabled Start. Automatic blocked Start again, and leaving/reopening New session reset the draft account. Reselecting it and clicking Start created a new chat and returned **`NEW_SESSION_ACCOUNT_OK`**. Exact-session metadata retained that account with source `user`; its owner-side successful-use timestamp advanced. Independent reads confirmed the default stayed cleared and preferences were unchanged. The original default was explicitly restored afterward without changing the chat pin.

A second verified person could not discover the saved account or freshly preview, create with, or select it. Exact owner denials, unchanged account/default inventories, unchanged complete bounded session-key/ID inventories, and absence of the attempted session were checked. The no-turn creation-denial probe did not invoke inference.

![New session account selection inside the model picker, without changing the saved default](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/249c9aab-4453-4eb5-808b-8db7ad10ac81)

![Actual Claude reply from the newly created, personally pinned chat](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a6c9278e-9099-4983-936b-c2a8585cdb7a)

The normal built Gateway had clean exact-head source, matching build-info, and a full served-asset manifest. Regression suites passed: **212 Gateway tests, 198 UI tests, and 13 mock-Gateway Playwright cases**, plus the affected cleanup reruns and canonical type/lint/native/guard checks. The real provider proof is separate from those mocked UI cases. The build passed; independent Codex review was scoped-clean at P0. All owned runtime/browser/credential-copy resources were cleaned up, and the intentionally saved credential was retained.

Review feedback for a later merge: keep the distinction between account selection and billing, complete the provider credential-use assessment, and retain the recorded cancellation/failover/refresh/Custodian gaps. A separate automatic-title observation remains: this synthetic exact-reply prompt produced a refusal-like title despite its correct chat answer. Its title-generation owner, not account selection, needs baseline investigation. These results do not constitute merge approval or an exact-head CI claim.

The PR body now includes the current proof, before/after screenshots, scope limits, and change accounting. Historical Claude sign-in/sticky-chat results and the original missing-picker evidence remain below.

<details>
<summary>Prior Claude proof and historical gap at 912f738, before this follow-up</summary>

## Claude live proof and remaining UI gap

I completed the personal Claude setup-token flow through real Chrome, Profile, and the normal built Gateway/CLI/UI. Source context is `912f738198223be74286181528ac5902e068e460`. The official, unmodified Claude CLI was **2.1.236**, verified by publisher signature and source/copy hash. The isolated fixture had no shared provider credential; native Claude reported `loggedIn: false` / `authMethod: none` both before and after the test.

The approved browser flow issued a fresh subscription setup-token. Profile accepted it, and all seven CLI list/use/clear-default/restore operations passed. Actual `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` replies:

| Scenario | Rendered reply | UI duration / output tokens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Personal new-chat default | `CLAUDE_PERSONAL_OK` | 2s / 81 |
| Same chat after clearing that default | `CLAUDE_STICKY_OK` | 1s / 49 |
| Explicit personal selection in a previously unused, addressable main chat | `CLAUDE_EXPLICIT_OK` | 4s / 148 |

Each completed personal turn advanced the exact saved credential owner's successful-use timestamp. After the third turn, independent CLI readback still showed one retained account and **zero personal defaults**. I then restored the original default. A second authenticated gateway person could neither list that account nor select its exact ID: the CLI returned the owner-specific refusal, and both inventories/defaults remained unchanged. These are credential-use and isolation observations, not billing receipts.

![Real Claude reply with an explicit personal account selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22a26156-0de9-47d3-84d0-cf62627d39de)

**Remaining follow-up: personal account selection before creating a session.** With the personal default cleared and no shared auth, `/new` allows drafting text but disables Start. Its model menu shows “Sign-in needed” and has no account picker. The retained account works through the existing-chat picker, but that does not prove the fresh-draft path. The disabled gate is correct; the missing recovery/selection surface is the problem. [New session's shared-control call](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/912f738198223be74286181528ac5902e068e460/ui/src/pages/new-session/model-control.ts#L599) lacks the account-control hook supplied by [existing chat](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/912f738198223be74286181528ac5902e068e460/ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-session-controls.ts#L139). Those New session files are outside this PR's diff. The follow-up should add an owner-authorized draft account selection/metadata preview, preserve readiness checks, and prove creation with the default still cleared. No fresh-draft inference occurred in this run.

![New session cannot choose the retained personal account with its default cleared](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6cd4bef2-3b2c-4b02-9c94-846d719d7b02)

The sign-in email's magic link signed in directly in this run; no copied verification code was needed. The setup-token callback was dynamic localhost, and the CLI completed with zero stdin submissions. All task-owned processes/listeners, test tabs, isolated state, and temporary credential captures were cleaned up. The intentionally saved credential remains in approved secret storage. One separate observation is recorded for follow-up: a synthetic Claude chat acquired a refusal-like automatic title; title generation was not investigated here.

Scope limits: UI credential entry was tested, not the hidden CLI credential-entry prompt; live shared failover, valid late-callback rejection, exchange cancellation, expiry/refresh, and personal-only Custodian startup remain unproved. The built UI retained its precommit label; all 101 recorded source-file hashes matched the candidate, which is not independent full-tree build-provenance verification. No production files or configuration were changed in this test pass, and the PR remains open.

Technical success also does not settle the provider-contract question. Anthropic's current [authentication and credential-use documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance#authentication-and-credential-use) distinguishes end-user sign-in to the unmodified CLI from third-party credential storage/intermediation. The PR's stored-token design needs that separate maintainer check; a successful reply or historical staff comment is not permission evidence.

Sibling Codex contracts were rechecked directly at `eb10d91e48ccbd0930427461fb392337addb1ac0`: [user/workspace claims](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/eb10d91e48ccbd0930427461fb392337addb1ac0/codex-rs/login/src/token_data.rs#L29), [callback listener ownership](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/eb10d91e48ccbd0930427461fb392337addb1ac0/codex-rs/login/src/server.rs#L620), and [PKCE exchange](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/eb10d91e48ccbd0930427461fb392337addb1ac0/codex-rs/login/src/server.rs#L809). This is source inspection, not an additional Codex live run.

</details>

The pre-provider-I/O finding was real and is repaired in `926fae23b475389021e4fa8077f331fc3aa84e0c`. The Gateway now passes its **original operation-owned authority assertion** through provider authentication to the shared final request-dispatch boundary. OpenAI and xAI revalidate after awaited preparation and on redirects; cancellation and final private-store checks remain separate protections.

The exact-head normal-Gateway test held an installed synthetic provider immediately before token and poll HTTP requests. After real role revocation closed the initiating socket, both retired operations made **zero requests and zero private writes**. Restored-writer controls each made one request and saved a synthetic account. There were **zero status requests during the holds**. The same probe on the prior `2841` head reached both forbidden sinks. All owned test processes, ports and private state were cleaned up.

The exact-head build, **319 focused auth tests in 14 files**, and real-Gateway browser hot-policy replay passed. Independent reviews cover the authority repair and subsequent integration fixes, including Dashboard iframe retention and request-owned worker retirement. The PR body maps all 12 items from the 11:16 UTC ClawSweeper review to their disposition and preserves the trust, storage, upgrade and billing limits.

Public xAI discovery passed through HTTP proxies and an independent NO_PROXY control. SOCKS traversal failed because of the already tracked shared transport defect in #131354, with separate repair #131436; its helper is unchanged from stable/current main. That failed matrix is not relabeled green. None of these results claims fresh external OAuth acceptance, inference or billing.

The two new Dashboard before/after screenshots are attached alongside the retained UI evidence. Required exact-head CI and native landing gates remain mandatory.

nodes.body:
### Disposition of the 12:52 UTC review on `926fae23`

The refreshed review reports no concrete implementation finding. Its missing Codex checkout is a reviewer-environment limitation, not an unperformed maintainer check: **I personally inspected the sibling Codex source at `94cbbddafc1776d5e377bca1b05932c697e82238`**, including the following contracts (and rechecked them during landing):

- [Account protocol](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/94cbbddafc1776d5e377bca1b05932c697e82238/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/account.rs#L63) and [account processor](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/94cbbddafc1776d5e377bca1b05932c697e82238/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/account_processor.rs#L288): API-key login writes the selected Codex credential store and reloads auth (lines 402–440); external-token login checks the configured workspace and replaces live auth (lines 826–879). It is not an OpenClaw human-authority boundary. The external-token variant is marked experimental upstream; this is an implementation-contract observation, not a new provider approval or stable-API guarantee.
- [Thread start parameters](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/94cbbddafc1776d5e377bca1b05932c697e82238/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread.rs#L62) and [turn start parameters](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/94cbbddafc1776d5e377bca1b05932c697e82238/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/turn.rs#L152): omitted turn fields inherit thread state; an empty environment selection disables it. OpenClaw must preserve the admitted model/environment rather than silently replace it at turn dispatch.
- [Interrupt handling](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/94cbbddafc1776d5e377bca1b05932c697e82238/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/turn_processor.rs#L1590) and [compaction](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/94cbbddafc1776d5e377bca1b05932c697e82238/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs#L2345): startup interruption has a distinct empty-turn contract; compaction operates on an existing thread. Neither supplies the initiating Gateway identity's live authorization.

The corresponding OpenClaw [physical-write boundary](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/926fae23b475389021e4fa8077f331fc3aa84e0c/extensions/codex/src/app-server/client.ts#L688) rechecks the retained assertion after waits/retries, synchronously before writing. [Auth handoff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/926fae23b475389021e4fa8077f331fc3aa84e0c/extensions/codex/src/app-server/auth-bridge.ts#L839) carries it into login; native user-home accounts are verified, not silently logged into. Earlier runtime regression/review receipts and the exact-head CI cover these adapters; this is not a new live external-auth claim.

Owner decision is explicitly recorded: the requesting maintainer approved this provider-neutral personal-account product and directed landing. The accepted contract is a trusted shared Gateway, identity-scoped credentials, defaults captured only for new sessions, sticky existing pins, documented same-provider shared fallback, and **selection is not an invoice/billing receipt**. Clearing defaults retains saved credentials/pins; provider revocation is separate. No new operator config/env option, SQLite schema/version, or protocol-version bump is introduced by the final repairs. The flagged UI cache is ephemeral WeakMap/Map state, not a persistent schema. Existing older-writer/reopen and session-preservation evidence remains attributed.

These facts address the eight review items and both rank-up moves concerning source inspection, owner acceptance and compatibility. Exact-head CI/native gates still must finish; the bot's confidence label is not represented as a new approval, and no duplicate re-review is requested.

Merged via squash.
